== con-leche/ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean#L90-L117
    90  /-- **The main theorem.**  Every environment the checker accepts has a
    91  model in every set theory — at every `Nat.div`/`Nat.mod` pin list, so
    92  consistency does not depend on which variants the install gate is
    93  handed (the empty list included: under it every stream that declares
    94  `Nat.div` declines).  The shipped binary runs the fold at
    95  `natOpPinSets`. -/
    96  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
    97      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (ds : Array Declaration) (env : Env)
    98      (accepted : checkDecls .verified pins ds = .ok env) :
    99      Nonempty (Model V env) := by
   100    obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) rfl accepted
   101    exact ⟨Model.Model.ofEnvModelM m⟩
   102  
   103  open Frontend in
   104  /-- **The main corollary.**  A file declaring a theorem of type `False`
   105  in the shape `jsonWithTheoremFalse` describes is rejected: the parse
   106  reads the template's four lines into a theorem record of type `False`,
   107  the preparation keeps the record, and a stream holding it is never
   108  accepted.  At every pin list, as the main theorem: the shipped binary
   109  runs the fold at `natOpPinSets`. -/
   110  theorem no_False_declaration (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
   111      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (chunks : List ByteArray)
   112      (h : jsonWithTheoremFalse chunks) :
   113      ∃ e, (do
   114        let pre ← builtinPreludeE
   115        let r ← parseChunks chunks
   116        let ds := preparePrelude pre r.decls
   117        checkDecls .verified pins ds) = .error e := by

== con-leche/ConLeche/Verify/Cached/MainC.lean#L36-L42
    36  /-- **Acceptance**: what the fold accepts carries the model. -/
    37  theorem checkDecls_sound (hμ : μ.verifiedChecks = true)
    38      {ds : Array Declaration} {env' : Env}
    39      (h : checkDecls μ pins ds = .ok env') :
    40      Nonempty (EnvModelM V μ env') := by
    41    obtain ⟨fc, rfl⟩ := checkDecls_fullyChecked μ h
    42    exact fullyChecked_sound V hμ fc

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L88-L210
    88  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
    89                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
    90                 FILE.ndjson
    91         con-ron --help
    92  
    93    (C), the Rust arena checker of con-ron's DESIGN.md section 8: con-leche's
    94    pure checker over an append-only DAG of per-constructor handle arrays, with
    95    con-leche's command line and con-leche's exit codes, so that
    96    scripts/diff-e2e.sh can run the same 383 fixtures against this binary and
    97    the Lean twin `con-ron-lean` alike.  A term is a u32 handle into a Vec: on
    98    the checking path there is no Arc, no tagged pointer and no reference count
    99    at all.  (The PINNED DATA the checker compares against is still
   100    con-leche's own constants as Expr values, interned into the persistent tier
   101    once at startup -- crates/con-ron-core/src/lib.rs says why.)
   102  
   103    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   104                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   105                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists), so a stream
   106                      declaring a theorem of type False is never accepted.  The
   107                      same two statements are PROVED about this program's
   108                      pipeline (ConRon.Capstone.model_exists and
   109                      no_False_declaration, on the Aeneas model of the Rust),
   110                      using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and
   111                      Quot.sound.  What they still assume are hypotheses, not
   112                      axioms: that the driver runs the extracted stages in the
   113                      order it does on the file's bytes.  They hold at every pin
   114                      text and every prelude.  OVERVIEW.md section 3.1 lists
   115                      them.
   116    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   117                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   118                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   119    --jobs=<n>        the check phase runs on <n> worker threads sharing the
   120                      persistent tier and the installed index by reference
   121                      (DESIGN.md section 8.3): each worker owns a scratch tier,
   122                      its own caches and a copy of the pin handles, and the
   123                      results are merged by record index and walked in record
   124                      order, so the verdict and the record a rejection names are
   125                      the same at every <n>.  Default: one per hardware thread,
   126                      capped at 16.  A worker reserves 1 GiB of stack, which a
   127                      `ulimit -v` must allow for.  0 or a non-numeral is a usage
   128                      error, as in con-leche.
   129    --no-mark-persistent
   130                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP, for a stronger reason than the
   131                      `con-ron` binary's: the mark it turns off is a
   132                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   133                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this checker has no
   134                      reference counts at all -- a term is a u32 handle into a
   135                      Vec and the persistent tier is immutable in phase B.  A
   136                      run that passes it says so on stderr.
   137    --progress[=<stride>]
   138                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   139                      phase:
   140                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   141                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   142                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> pending
   143                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   144                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   145                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s
   146                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   147                      declaration is installed, so a run that dies in the
   148                      install phase names the declaration it died in on its last
   149                      line; a check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th
   150                      COMPLETED check.  On a failure the phase's closing line
   151                      says so and the summary still prints.  Bare --progress is
   152                      stride 1; a stride that is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is
   153                      a usage error.
   154    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   155                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   156                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.  The pins
   157                      are interned into the persistent tier at startup, before
   158                      the fold (DESIGN.md section 8.6 P2d).
   159    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   160                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream
   161                      declines.  Neither flag is needed for a normal run: the
   162                      pins are con-leche's `natOpPinSets`, embedded in the
   163                      verified core and decoded by it.  A run with either
   164                      flag is outside the proved theorems.
   165    --help            print this text on STDOUT and exit 0, in any argument
   166                      position; no input is read.  Its last line names the
   167                      global allocator THIS binary was built with (below), so a
   168                      measurement can be reproduced.
   169  
   170  build-time selection (cargo features, not command-line flags): the global
   171  allocator is `con-ron-dump`'s `#[global_allocator]`, chosen on this crate's
   172  dependency edge -- `cargo build --release` is mimalloc, `--no-default-features`
   173  is glibc `malloc`, and `--no-default-features --features jemalloc` is jemalloc.
   174  It is the same edge `crates/con-ron` has, so the two checkers are measured on
   175  the same allocator unless a build says otherwise.
   176  
   177  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   178  exits 3 without reading its input.
   179  
   180  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.
   181  An out-of-memory condition is NEITHER: this program aborts the way Rust aborts
   182  on a failed allocation ('memory allocation of <n> bytes failed', SIGABRT,
   183  which a shell reports as 134).  A panic is exit 3.
   184  
   185  THE VERDICT LINE'S COUNT.  It counts the FILE's accepted declaration RECORDS:
   186  one per def/theorem/opaque/axiom/inductive/quot record the file declares.  The
   187  built-in prelude's own records are not counted; a stream record that declares
   188  a prelude declaration IS counted.  That count is a property of the INPUT; the
   189  number of environment CONSTANTS is not.
   190  
   191  THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE.  Every run installs, first and unconditionally, the
   192  checker's own little prelude -- the five pinned basis blocks (Eq, Nat, Empty,
   193  False, Quot) and the toolchain's Bool and And blocks, embedded at build
   194  time -- so the pin-certified Nat operations find their ground whatever order
   195  the export chose.  It is parsed into the SAME store as the stream, which is
   196  what the persistent tier is for: the prelude's nodes and the stream's are
   197  hash-consed together.
   198  
   199  NO PREPROCESSOR, NO MODELS.  The input is a RAW lean4export stream: there is no
   200  external tool, no dependency and no spawn.  Every inductive block --
   201  structures, sums, indexed families, recursive, reflexive, mutual and nested
   202  blocks -- is installed by the ONE uniform installer: it checks the type formers
   203  and constructors, runs the positivity check, and GENERATES the block's
   204  recursors; the stream's recursor records supply only their types, compared with
   205  the generated ones up to definitional equality, and their classes -- the rule
   206  bodies the stream carries are ignored.  No model is ever read from the input: a
   207  stream record whose name carries a `_model` component is an ordinary
   208  declaration with no effect on any block.  A block whose shape the installer
   209  does not recognise declines (exit 2), naming it.  The binary reads no
   210  environment variable.";

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L13-L132
    13  /-!
    14  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    15  
    16  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    17  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    18  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    19  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's two headline theorems in the shape
    20  the original campaign used (`conron.model_exists` /
    21  `conron.no_False_declaration`, `proof/ConRon/RefineOld/Main.lean`):
    22  
    23  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — every environment the Aeneas model of the
    24    Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    25  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    26    type `False` is never accepted by it.
    27  
    28  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    29  frontier is measured as the dependency closure of these two, and it is
    30  EMPTY since `arena` `db1131f1` (task #97-MILESTONE): both depend on
    31  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` only (§5's census).  What they
    32  still assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    33  
    34  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    35  
    36  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    37  around six extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    38  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    39  
    40      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    41        → prepare_prelude → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the declaration fold)
    42  
    43  The headlines (§4) take one premise per call, from the binary's own start
    44  values `startState`/`emptyTier` (§3); §4's table maps each premise to its line
    45  of `check_main`.
    46  
    47  and the twin runs the same six stages (`Arena/Main.lean`'s
    48  `runPipelineHead`/`runPipelineTail` drive them for `con-ron-lean`).  **The sixth stage is the fold the
    49  binary's driver runs, pool and all** (task #97-P5-POOL):
    50  `driver::check_decls_driver` runs phase A with the heartbeat as its hook,
    51  freezes the tier, runs phase B on `pool::parallel_all`, and thaws the tier.
    52  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` phase A, `h7` the freeze, `h8`
    53  phase B), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles into
    54  `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  Phase B's premise `h8` is
    55  the contract of the generic combinator `pool::parallel_all` with the driver's
    56  two verified closures, written out (task #98-H8): index lists `ws`, one per
    57  worker, covering every pending record, and for each a `foldlM` of
    58  `check_pending` over its indices from `worker_state`, accepting.  That
    59  contract is the pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of
    60  `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.  `parallelAll_of_pool` reads it as
    61  `Phased.lean`'s `ParallelAll`, and `PoolAccepts.toParts` turns that into one
    62  accepting fold per worker over the records it checked.
    63  The theorems hold for EVERY install hook, so they cover the plain run and
    64  `--progress` alike.  `pool_accepts_refines` relates the stage to the twin's
    65  `Arena.PooledAccepts`, and `Bridge/Checker/Phased.lean`'s
    66  `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` carries that to the pure fold.  So the
    67  statement takes the six Rust RUNS as premises (that the binary's
    68  `check_main` makes exactly these calls, in this order, is the one trusted
    69  line, exactly as it was for the original campaign), and the proof is:
    70  
    71  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s six `…_refines` lemmas walk the
    72     Rust runs into six TWIN runs from the twin's own start state
    73     `AState.init EStore.empty`, related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/
    74     `AStateInv`: lockstep);
    75  2. **Theorem 1** — the twin runs feed `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`, whose
    76     pure fold accepts the denoted stream: con-leche's
    77     `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` gives the model, and
    78     `no_False_theorem_accepted_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream
    79     (`stages_no_False`, through the pure fold);
    80  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a
    81     model.
    82  
    83  Every step is an existing theorem; what this file adds is glue: the Rust
    84  runs threaded through `Sim₀`/`SimStream`/`SimFold`, and the one twin-store
    85  fact the composition needs from Theorem 1 — `StoreWF` at the headline's
    86  `AStateRel` (`stages_storeWF`) — read off its stage lemmas.  Theorem 2 itself
    87  carries no fact about the twin's store (task #97-T2-AUDIT).
    88  
    89  ## The named hypotheses
    90  
    91  Since task #98-HEADLINE the headlines start from the binary's own start
    92  values (`startState` = `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`)
    93  instead of quantifying over a start state with `hpers`/`hest`/`hst0`
    94  equations, name the call the binary makes at each step (`prepare_d`, not
    95  `prepare_prelude`).  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    96  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`), what
    97  they assume is exactly:
    98

    34  def ReadsAs {S : Type} (inst : frontend.export_c.ChunkSource S) :
    35      S → List (alloc.vec.Vec Std.U8) → Prop
    36    | src, [] => ∃ e src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (e, src') ∧ e.val = []
    37    | src, c :: cs => c.val ≠ [] ∧
    38        ∃ src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (c, src') ∧ ReadsAs inst src' cs

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L15
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle:
     5  //!
     6  //! ```text
     7  //! bits 31…28   ctor tag   (4 bits, high)
     8  //! bit  27      tier       (0 = persistent, 1 = scratch)
     9  //! bits 26…0    index      into THAT CONSTRUCTOR'S array of THAT TIER
    10  //! ```
    11  //!
    12  //! so 134 217 728 nodes per constructor per tier, and — the point of putting
    13  //! the tier *above* the index rather than in the low bit (con-leche's lesson
    14  //! 6) — a persistent handle's bits never change when the scratch tier comes
    15  //! and goes.

   166  /// into the **binder datum store**: the same word layout as the other four (tag
   167  /// 0, the tier bit, the index), for a store with ONE constructor and so no tag
   168  /// to spend.

   172  /// a `PropWhen` is `Arc`-carrying at `one`/`two`/`many`, so every `dup2` of a
   173  /// binder record is a reference count and every cons probe of the binder
   174  /// tables compares one (task #97-P6-10 §3 priced the pair at 2–3 % of
   175  /// `Init`).  With the datum interned the record is three `u32`s of POD, its
   176  /// hash is `pack2`-shaped like the other nine, and its `eq2` is three word
   177  /// comparisons.

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L4110-L4145
  4110      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:501-521 EStore.intern
  4111      /// Hash-cons an expression node: probe the persistent cons table, then the
  4112      /// scratch one, then append to the tier the store is in (DESIGN.md §8.3).
  4113      /// The cap test is the Lean's `capOK` turned into the `Native` decline
  4114      /// §8.3 puts here.
  4115      ///
  4116      /// **Dispatched ONCE** (task #97-P6-15).  The body below used to run the
  4117      /// whole sequence over the `ENodeView`, and each of its four steps
  4118      /// dispatched on the view's tag again and built the node record again:
  4119      /// the persistent probe built it (inside `ETables::find`), the scratch
  4120      /// probe built it a second time, `der_of_view` re-dispatched to compute
  4121      /// the derived word, and `ETables::push` re-dispatched and built it a
  4122      /// third time to append it.  A binder paid `binder_meta_dup` at each of
  4123      /// the three.  So the tag is read once here and the ten per-constructor
  4124      /// paths below each build their record ONCE and hand the same `&r` to the
  4125      /// two probes, to the capacity test and to the push — the same clauses in
  4126      /// the same order, with the dispatch and the two rebuilds gone.
  4127      ///
  4128      /// The twin's `intern` is one `def` over `ENodeView`; what is owed is the
  4129      /// ten-arm spelling and `internC v = intern (view of C)` per constructor,
  4130      /// each of them `rfl` after the `match`.
  4131      pub fn intern(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, v: ENodeView) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  4132          match v {
  4133              ENodeView::BVar(i) => self.intern_bvar(pers, i),
  4134              ENodeView::FVar(idx, ty) => self.intern_fvar(pers, idx, ty),
  4135              ENodeView::Sort(u) => self.intern_sort(pers, u),
  4136              ENodeView::Const(n, us) => self.intern_const(pers, n, us),
  4137              ENodeView::App(f, a) => self.intern_app(pers, f, a),
  4138              ENodeView::Lam(ty, body, m) => self.intern_lam(pers, ty, body, m),
  4139              ENodeView::ForallE(ty, body, m) => self.intern_forall_e(pers, ty, body, m),
  4140              ENodeView::LetE(ty, val, body) => self.intern_let_e(pers, ty, val, body),
  4141              ENodeView::Lit(l) => self.intern_lit(pers, l),
  4142              ENodeView::Proj(n, i, e) => self.intern_proj(pers, n, i, e),
  4143          }
  4144      }
  4145

  4395      pub fn intern_app(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, f: EIdx, a: EIdx) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  4396          let r: AppNode = AppNode { f, a };
  4397          let sk: bool = if self.scratch_on {
  4398              if r.f.is_persistent() {
  4399                  !r.a.is_persistent()
  4400              } else {
  4401                  true
  4402              }
  4403          } else {
  4404              false
  4405          };
  4406          let hit: Option<EIdx> = if sk {
  4407              None
  4408          } else if pers.frozen {
  4409              pers.e.apps.find(&r)
  4410          } else {
  4411              self.pers.apps.find(&r)
  4412          };
  4413          match hit {
  4414              Some(hp) => Ok(hp),
  4415              None => {
  4416                  if self.scratch_on {
  4417                      let at: (usize, Option<EIdx>) = self.scr.apps.find_slot(&r);
  4418                      match at.1 {
  4419                          Some(hs) => Ok(hs),
  4420                          None => {
  4421                              if self.scr.apps.full() {
  4422                                  Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  4423                              } else {
  4424                                  let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  4425                                  let h: EIdx =
  4426                                      EIdx::pack(ETAG_APP, TIER_S, self.scr.apps.size() as u32);
  4427                                  self.scr.apps.push_at(at.0, r, d, h.dup2());
  4428                                  Ok(h)
  4429                              }
  4430                          }
  4431                      }
  4432                  } else if self.pers.apps.full() {
  4433                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  4434                  } else {
  4435                      let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  4436                      let h: EIdx = EIdx::pack(ETAG_APP, TIER_P, self.pers.apps.size() as u32);
  4437                      self.pers.apps.push(r, d, h.dup2());
  4438                      Ok(h)
  4439                  }
  4440              }
  4441          }

 11735  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/StateC.lean:319-326 CState.flushed
 11736  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3961-3967 flushCaches` — **what
 11737  /// the per-declaration bracket does to the caches**: it drops them whole,
 11738  /// which is con-leche's own `flushC`, the operation its driver runs at exactly
 11739  /// this point.
 11740  ///
 11741  /// Task #97-P4c ported DESIGN.md §8.3's survivor policy instead — keep the
 11742  /// rows whose key AND value are persistent — which is sound and strictly more
 11743  /// caching; task #97f measured what it costs (`filter` is `O(table)` and the
 11744  /// survivors accumulate, so the fold pays `O(declarations × surviving rows)`:
 11745  /// 16 % of `Init`'s first 4 380 declarations' cycles, 213 s → 124 s).  The
 11746  /// twin's `Caches.dropScratchEntries` stays as the SPECIFICATION of a
 11747  /// surviving row, and so does `Caches::drop_scratch_entries` below it with
 11748  /// its eleven journals — P3 needs it to state that flushing is sound.
 11749  pub fn flush_caches(st: &mut AState) {
 11750      st.caches.reset();
 11751  }
 11752  
 11753  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, closed** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 11754  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3969-3977 dropScratch` — drop the
 11755  /// scratch tier of the store and the cache entries that name it, in one
 11756  /// operation, so the two halves cannot drift apart; and **thaw** the store:
 11757  /// the tier `enter_scratch` handed out comes back (task #98-FREEZE), so the
 11758  /// store is owned and scratch-off again.
 11759  pub fn drop_scratch(st: &mut AState, tier: PersTier) {
 11760      flush_caches(st);
 11761      st.store.thaw(tier);
 11762  }
 11763  
 11764  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, opened** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 11765  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3979-3986 enterScratch` — turn the
 11766  /// scratch tier on, and clear the per-call memo tables of `Memos`, which
 11767  /// belong to no tier and whose keys the new tier may reuse.  **Opening a
 11768  /// bracket is freezing the store** (task #98-FREEZE): its persistent tables
 11769  /// are handed back as the `PersTier` every read inside the bracket goes
 11770  /// through and promotion writes, and every append inside it is a scratch
 11771  /// append.
 11772  pub fn enter_scratch(st: &mut AState) -> PersTier {
 11773      st.memos.reset();
 11774      st.store.freeze()
 11775  }

     1  //! `arena::promote` — the scratch → persistent copy (DESIGN.md §8.3, task #97-P6-2).
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Promote.lean`, declaration for
     4  //! declaration, under DESIGN.md §8.6's lockstep ruling.
     5  //!
     6  //! DESIGN.md §8.3, "**Phase A runs in the scratch tier too, with promotion**":
     7  //!
     8  //! > The install phase (annotate the type and the value, infer, defeq) was
     9  //! > interning every intermediate into the persistent tier — on `Init` 5.06 M
    10  //! > permanent nodes on top of the parse's 6.14 M (+82 %) […].  The arena's
    11  //! > answer is con-leche #64's: phase A opens the scratch tier like phase B,
    12  //! > and the two handles it must keep (the annotated type, the annotated
    13  //! > value) are **promoted** — a memoised structural copy scratch →
    14  //! > persistent […] before the tier is dropped.  Persistent handles are
    15  //! > promoted to themselves.
    16  //!
    17  //! This module is that copy, at all four handle kinds and lifted to
    18  //! `arena::env`'s declaration layer, plus `promote_new` — the entry
    19  //! `arena::checker`'s two fold steps call, which promotes a step's NEWLY
    20  //! INSTALLED constants in place.
    21  //!
    22  //! ## What it is
    23  //!
    24  //! `view` the node, promote its children, `intern` the result into the
    25  //! PERSISTENT tier (`arena::store`'s `intern_persistent` family, whose section
    26  //! note carries the WF obligations).  Three properties make it cheap and make
    27  //! it right:
    28  //!
    29  //! * **a persistent handle promotes to itself**, by one tier-bit test
    30  //!   (`is_persistent`) and no store access at all.  Most of an annotated term
    31  //!   IS the parsed term — `annotate` rebuilds only the spine it changes — so
    32  //!   the walk stops at the first persistent node on every branch;
    33  //! * **the memo makes it `O(result)`** and not `O(unfolding)`: the subject is
    34  //!   a hash-consed DAG, and an unmemoised structural copy of a DAG is the
    35  //!   mistake task #97g's item 5 found three times over.  The memo is per
    36  //!   DECLARATION — a scratch handle means nothing once the tier is dropped —
    37  //!   and it is threaded as an argument-and-result pair, a moved
    38  //!   `ron::HashMap` returned, which is `frontend::proj_rec`'s spelling for its
    39  //!   `seen` set and `arena::expr_ops`' for the three memoized scope walks;
    40  //! * **`intern_persistent` probes the persistent cons table first**, so

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L667-L689
   667  /// con-leche: none — the phase boundary, which con-leche has no tier to make
   668  /// Lean twin: none — the twin has no tier to move; its phase-B worker reads the
   669  /// persistent tier where it is (`AState.worker`, `Arena/Phased.lean`).
   670  /// **The persistent tier out of the store and into a value** (task
   671  /// #97-P6-6b's driver function, moved here by task #97-P5-Driver): the four
   672  /// persistent tables move into one `PersTier` handed back `frozen`, for the
   673  /// phase-B workers to read.  Task #98-FREEZE: this is a pure MOVE — the
   674  /// store's scratch tiers and flags are untouched (a worker's store is its own,
   675  /// `worker_state`), there is no flag to test and so no decline (`M_REFREEZE`
   676  /// is gone), and `thaw_tier` puts the tables back where they were.  The
   677  /// driver's store is not read between the two.
   678  pub fn freeze_tier(ar: &mut EStore) -> PersTier {
   679      let n: NTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.ns.pers, NTables::empty());
   680      let l: LTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.pers, LTables::empty());
   681      let ls: LsTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.pers, LsTables::empty());
   682      let e: ETables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.pers, ETables::empty());
   683      PersTier {
   684          frozen: true,
   685          n,
   686          l,
   687          ls,
   688          e,
   689      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core_state.rs#L453-L500
   453  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-PERF-WALKMEMO)
   454  /// The slot count past which `take_walk_memo` hands back a FRESH table
   455  /// instead of a cleared one; see its note for how the value was chosen.
   456  pub const WALK_MEMO_KEEP: usize = 1 << 16;
   457  
   458  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean:395-397 Expr.allLevelParamsDefinedFast
   459  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/DeclCheck.lean:190-192 Expr.constsResolveFFast
   460  /// Lean twin: the `∅` that `proof/ConRon/Arena/CheckerBase.lean`'s
   461  /// `allLevelParamsDefined` and `constsResolveFFast` start their walk from —
   462  /// **the parked walk memo, moved out of the state and emptied** (task
   463  /// #97-PERF-WALKMEMO).  The slot is left holding `HashMap::new()` (which
   464  /// allocates nothing) for the length of the walk, and the entry puts the
   465  /// grown table back afterwards; either way the table this returns is empty,
   466  /// so the walk starts where the twin's does.
   467  ///
   468  /// **nanoda's guard** (`nanoda_lib/src/expr.rs`, `inst`): a table past
   469  /// `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` slots is dropped rather than kept, so that one huge walk
   470  /// does not leave a huge table behind for every later call.  `reset_map`'s
   471  /// `clear_fit` already decays such a table, one eighth of its high-water mark
   472  /// a call, so the guard only decides which of the two is cheaper for an
   473  /// outlier: re-growing from nothing, or `clear_fit`'s re-make at the decayed
   474  /// size.  The threshold, measured on `Init` (`--verified --jobs=1`, one
   475  /// `perf stat -e instructions:u` run each, all accepting 57 977):
   476  ///
   477  /// | `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` | instructions:u |
   478  /// |---|---:|
   479  /// | fresh `HashMap::new()` per call (before) | 211 976 016 505 |
   480  /// | 2^10 slots (nanoda's 1024) | 208 379 555 799 |
   481  /// | 2^12 | 206 572 063 910 |
   482  /// | 2^14 | 205 851 105 938 |
   483  /// | **2^16** | **205 785 515 243** |
   484  /// | no guard (2^60) | 205 783 023 575 |
   485  ///
   486  /// A guard low enough to trip on ordinary calls gives the saving back — at
   487  /// nanoda's 1024 more than half of it — because those calls re-grow by
   488  /// doubling, which is exactly the cost this table exists to avoid.  2^16 is
   489  /// the smallest power tried that costs nothing measurable on `Init` (2.5 M
   490  /// instructions over no guard), so it only ever fires on an outlier.
   491  pub fn take_walk_memo<K, V>(slot: &mut HashMap<K, V>) -> HashMap<K, V> {
   492      let m: HashMap<K, V> = core::mem::replace(slot, HashMap::new());
   493      if m.capacity() > WALK_MEMO_KEEP {
   494          HashMap::new()
   495      } else {
   496          let mut m2: HashMap<K, V> = m;
   497          reset_map(&mut m2);
   498          m2
   499      }
   500  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/hashmap2.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; a second `Std.HashMap` replacement, proved
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::HashMap2<K, V>` — proved in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean`
     4  //! (task #97-HM2; designed in task #97-P6-4b).  The same abstract object as
     5  //! `ron::hashmap`'s `HashMap` — a partial map from `K` to `V`, with
     6  //! `Hashable`/`Eq2`/`Dup` as its dictionaries and the same eleven operations
     7  //! — over an **open-addressed, epoch-stamped, flat slot vector** instead of
     8  //! the Aeneas tutorial's chained buckets.  `ron::hashmap` is untouched and
     9  //! keeps its proofs (`proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap.lean`); this module's are
    10  //! in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean` (task #97-HM2).
    11  //!
    12  //! **Why it exists.**  Task #97-P6-1 left `clear_slots + allocate_slots +
    13  //! move_elements*` at 21.8 % of `Init`, "all halving recursions over chained
    14  //! buckets".  Task #97-P6-4b counted what those recursions actually do on
    15  //! `Init`, and the counts name the representation rather than the code:
    16  //!
    17  //! | on `Init`, `ron::HashMap` | count |
    18  //! |---|---:|
    19  //! | `get` calls | 1 228 953 968 |
    20  //! | — resolved in 0 or 1 chain step | 98.8 % |
    21  //! | `insert` calls | 627 320 951 |
    22  //! | **`clear` calls** | **36 053 620** |
    23  //! | **— buckets walked by them** | **2 940 488 064** |
    24  //! | — entries those buckets held | 586 917 896 |
    25  //! | buckets pushed by `allocate_slots` | 948 184 512 |
    26  //! | entries moved by `move_elements*` | 349 323 629 |
    27  //!
    28  //! So the chains are *already* short — the table is a good hash table — and
    29  //! essentially all of the 21.8 % is the per-bucket cost of **emptying and
    30  //! re-growing** the slot vector: 2.94 G bucket writes to clear 0.59 G entries
    31  //! (five buckets walked per entry cleared; the average cleared table is 82
    32  //! buckets holding 16 entries) and 0.95 G `Vec::push`es to allocate them back.
    33  //! Nothing a better chain walk can do touches that.
    34  //!
    35  //! **The representation.**
    36  //!
    37  //! * `slots : Vec<Slot<K, V>>`, `Slot` = `Vacant | Live(u32, K, V)`.  No

   444              }

   483              return 3;
   484          }
   485      };

   495              st.store.ns().node_count(pers),

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/pins.rs#L1-L60
     1  //! `arena::pins` — the reserved names, interned ONCE (task #97-P6-4a).
     2  //!
     3  //! con-leche compares its reserved names — `natName`, `natZeroName`,
     4  //! `natSuccName`, the sixteen `Nat`-operation names, the `Bool` trio, the
     5  //! `String`/`List`/`Char` family, the standard and the trusted axiom names —
     6  //! as `Name` VALUES, which Lean builds once per nullary `def` and caches.
     7  //! The arena compares them as HANDLES, so `arena::core::pin` turned each one
     8  //! into `intern_name` of a freshly built `Name`: a `code_points` allocation
     9  //! and an `Arc<NameNode>` per path segment, then one cons-table probe per
    10  //! segment, every time.  Task #97-P6-1's counter measured what that costs on
    11  //! `Init`: **140 083 646 `NStore::intern` calls, of which 88 854 033 are
    12  //! probes of a `str` node built purely to be compared and dropped** — tens of
    13  //! millions of rebuilds of about forty constants, in `natLitSupported`'s
    14  //! three probes per literal, in `natOpNames`, in `strLitToConstructor`.
    15  //!
    16  //! This module is DESIGN.md's answer, flagged at task #97c ("the `Pins`
    17  //! record that is NOT here") and deferred there for want of a number: one
    18  //! record, filled once at the driver by `intern_reserved_pins`, and every
    19  //! `pin` of a constant name becomes a field read.
    20  //!
    21  //! **Not `arena::checker`'s `intern_all_pins`.**  That one walks the `--pins`
    22  //! RECEIPT file (the trusted pin list) into the persistent tier; this one
    23  //! interns the checker's own reserved constants.  The two run at the same
    24  //! point of the pipeline and mean different things, which is why they have
    25  //! different names.
    26  //!
    27  //! ## The table is a `Vec`, and that is what kills task #97c's hazard
    28  //!
    29  //! Task #97c declined the record because of an initialisation-order hazard:
    30  //! "a pin read before it is filled compares against the zero word and
    31  //! silently says *not `Nat`*".  A record of handle FIELDS has that hazard,
    32  //! because every 32-bit word is a syntactically valid handle.  A `Vec<NIdx>`
    33  //! does not: before `intern_reserved_pins` runs the table is EMPTY, so `pin_at`
    34  //! takes its bounds branch and raises `CheckError::Internal` — a loud stop,
    35  //! never a quiet wrong answer.  The cost is one `len` compare per read,
    36  //! against an interning walk it replaces.
    37  //!
    38  //! ## What is pinned
    39  //!
    40  //! The fifty names below and `basis_names::reserved_basis_names()`'s
    41  //! sixteen, plus the three interned values every `pin` site around them
    42  //! needs: the empty universe-argument list, the level `0` and the expression
    43  //! `Sort 1` (`arena::core`'s `empty_levels`, `zero_level` and `sort_one`,
    44  //! which now read this record instead of interning).
    45  //!
    46  //! All of them go into the PERSISTENT tier, because `intern_reserved_pins` runs
    47  //! before the parse, while the scratch tier is closed.  That matters twice:
    48  //! a pinned handle must survive every `drop_scratch` (it is read across all
    49  //! of them), and task #97-P6-1's `pers_find_maybe` rests on "a persistent
    50  //! node's children are persistent", which the bottom-up intern of a closed
    51  //! scratch tier gives for free.
    52  //!
    53  //! **Denotation unchanged.**  A pin is `intern_name` of the same `Name`, so
    54  //! the handle this record holds is the handle `pin` computed before —
    55  //! `denoteN` is injective and `intern` is idempotent, so pre-interning a name
    56  //! the export also carries hands the export's parse the very same handle.
    57  //! What changes is only WHEN the intern happens, and how many times.
    58  //!
    59  //! Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:117-134 AState` (DESIGN.md §8.6's
    60  //! twin ledger, task #97-P6-4a) — `AState` gains a `pins : Pins` field and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/prepare.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Prepare.lean` — **what happens between the
     2  //! file and the fold** (task #97 P4e part 1).
     3  //!
     4  //! `prepare_prelude` is total — no record of the stream is dropped, rewritten
     5  //! or retagged — and it does two things:
     6  //!
     7  //! 1. **the prelude's declarations first**, the stream's OWN copy of each
     8  //!    where the stream has one and a synthesised one only where it has none,
     9  //!    so a stream that declares the toolchain's `Bool` is checked on its own
    10  //!    `Bool` record;
    11  //! 2. **the ground hoist**: a pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
    12  //!    structural ground is moved ahead of it when the stream declares it
    13  //!    later.
    14  //!
    15  //! Moving a record earlier can only reject, never accept, which is why the
    16  //! spec con-leche proves is as simple as it is:
    17  //!
    18  //! ```text
    19  //! ∃ extra, (∀ d ∈ extra, d ∈ prelude) ∧
    20  //!   (preparePrelude ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra)
    21  //! ```
    22  //!
    23  //! **Step 2 is `frontend::nat_op_ground`'s**, a module of its own exactly as
    24  //! con-leche's is (task #97-P4d; task #97-P4e part 1 shipped an identity
    25  //! placeholder here, because the pass needs the kernel's
    26  //! `natOpNames`/`natDivModNames`, which arrived with the pins).  It is why
    27  //! `prepare_d` takes the whole `AState` where everything else in this module
    28  //! needs only the store.
    29  //!
    30  //! **Where the store comes from.**  Only `prelude_key`, whose `.anonymous`
    31  //! fall-through has to be INTERNED, and the two functions that call it;
    32  //! [`pick_idx`] and [`declares`] are pure, exactly as con-leche's are, because
    33  //! `env::i_declaration_names` is (`arena/env.rs`'s `table_name` note).
    34  //! Nothing in this module reads or writes a term.
    35  //!
    36  //! **The deviation of the port into the verified core** (task #84), kept
    37  //! verbatim from `con_ron_core::frontend::prepare`: con-leche's `pick` ERASES
    38  //! the picked record from the array (`Array.eraseIdxIfInBounds`) and `frontOf`
    39  //! moves it to the front.  The Aeneas subset has no operation that takes an
    40  //! element out of a `Vec` — no `remove`, no `pop`, no `into_iter` — so the
    41  //! port splits the two halves that con-leche fuses: [`pick_idx`] is the cited
    42  //! `ds.findIdx (declares n)` with the erasure recorded in a `picked` mask
    43  //! instead of performed, [`front_of`] runs that over the prelude, and
    44  //! [`prepared_stream`] materialises the whole prepared list in ONE pass.  The
    45  //! list that comes out is the same list; the cost is one record copy per
    46  //! record, where the copied fields are handles and `Vec` spines and not terms.
    47  //! con-leche's `pickSpec`/`frontSpec` are not ported (they are `cons`-list
    48  //! specifications with no caller on the run path); `pick_spec` lives in this
    49  //! module's tests, where it still checks `pick_idx` against the specification
    50  //! on every `cargo test`.

   741  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/BasisA.lean:48-54 BasisKind.declsA
   742  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:309-344 internAllPins` — **the
   743  /// one-time tree walk of DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d**: every datum the checker compares
   744  /// a stream record against, interned into the tier that is live at the call —
   745  /// which, at the driver's call, is the persistent one.
   746  ///
   747  /// The five basis blocks in both forms (the RAW ones `basis_pin_hit` and
   748  /// `quot_pin_hit` compare against, the ANNOTATED ones `check_basis_decl`
   749  /// installs), the standard and compiler-trust axiom pins, the reserved names
   750  /// the guards compare by handle, and the `Nat`-operation pin variants, whose
   751  /// interned form is the checker's pin-list parameter (con-leche's task #304).
   752  pub fn intern_all_pins(
   753      pers: &PersTier,

   755      pins: &Vec<NatOpPinSet>,

   763                  Ok(()) => intern_pin_sets(pers, st, pins, 0, Vec::new()),
   764              },
   765          },
   766      }
   767  }

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L942-L987
   942  // handle.  Only the READS are here, for `crate::driver`'s reason:
   943  // `IO.FS.Handle.read` has no model, and a theorem about the file is a
   944  // theorem about its bytes.
   945  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   946  
   947  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/Stream.lean:297-311 serialLoop
   948  /// **The file handle as the parse's `ChunkSource`**: each `next_chunk` is one
   949  /// `read_up_to` of `chunk` bytes, strictly forward, handed over whole; the
   950  /// first empty read is the end of the input.  A failed read ends the input
   951  /// the same way and is KEPT here, and `parse_export_handle_d` reports it in
   952  /// place of whatever the parse of the truncated input said — so a read error
   953  /// is exit 3, never a verdict, as before the loop moved.
   954  pub struct HandleSource<'a, R: Read> {
   955      /// The open reader.
   956      pub h: &'a mut R,
   957      /// The buffer size, `export_c::CHUNK_SIZE` in the binary.
   958      pub chunk: usize,
   959      /// The nonempty buffers handed out so far, for the heartbeat.
   960      pub chunks: u64,
   961      /// The first read failure, if any.
   962      pub err: Option<std::io::Error>,
   963  }
   964  
   965  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/Stream.lean:297-311 serialLoop
   966  impl<'a, R: Read> ChunkSource for HandleSource<'a, R> {
   967      /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/Stream.lean:297-311 serialLoop
   968      /// One read of up to `chunk` bytes; empty at the end or on a failure.
   969      fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
   970          if self.err.is_some() {
   971              return Vec::new();
   972          }
   973          let mut buf: Vec<u8> = vec![0u8; self.chunk];
   974          match read_up_to(self.h, &mut buf) {
   975              Ok(n) => {
   976                  buf.truncate(n);
   977                  if n > 0 {
   978                      self.chunks += 1;
   979                  }
   980                  buf
   981              }
   982              Err(e) => {
   983                  self.err = Some(e);
   984                  Vec::new()
   985              }
   986          }
   987      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! `arena::checker` — the declaration fold, over handles.
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean`, which is con-leche's
     4  //! `Kernel/Checker.lean`'s `checkDecl`/`checkDeclsPure` and
     5  //! `Cached/Installed.lean`'s two-phase `checkDecls`.
     6  //!
     7  //! ## Two folds, and which is which
     8  //!
     9  //! * **`check_decls_pure`** is the THEOREM's shape —
    10  //!   `ConLeche/Model/Fold.lean`'s `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` consumes it, and
    11  //!   DESIGN.md §8.2's Theorem 1 folds `checkDecl` over the stream.  One step
    12  //!   per record, install and check together.
    13  //! * **`install_then_check`** is what the BINARY runs: phase A installs every
    14  //!   record, annotating its header and its value but not inferring; phase B
    15  //!   checks each recorded declaration against the PREFIX VIEW it was installed
    16  //!   at.  con-leche proves the two are the same accept
    17  //!   (`fullyChecked_checkDecls`); the arena's two call the same `checkDecl`
    18  //!   pieces, which is what keeps them the same computation.
    19  //!
    20  //! ## Every step is bracketed
    21  //!
    22  //! DESIGN.md §8.3: "Persistent = parse + installed environment; scratch = one
    23  //! declaration's check."  Both phases and both folds run each record inside
    24  //! `enter_scratch` … `drop_scratch`.  Phase B's `check_pending` brackets
    25  //! `check_value_group`, and every node it appends goes with the tier.  Phase
    26  //! A's `annot_step` brackets the install too (the fallback `annot_step_other`
    27  //! included), because annotation infers and inference interns: `promote`
    28  //! copies exactly what leaves the step — the installed constants and the
    29  //! pending record — to the persistent tier before the drop (see `annot_step`).
    30  //! `check_decls_pure`'s step, `check_decl_step`, is bracketed the same way.
    31  //!
    32  //! ## The pins are interned at startup
    33  //!
    34  //! `intern_all_pins` is DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d's one-time tree walk, and it is what
    35  //! makes every later `pin`/`intern_ci` of the same datum return the PERSISTENT
    36  //! handle whatever tier is live (§8.3: `intern` probes the persistent table
    37  //! first).  Without it a reserved name first interned inside a scratch tier
    38  //! would compare unequal to the stream's own persistent copy of it, which is
    39  //! the one way hash-consing can go wrong across the tier boundary.
    40  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L225-L265
   225  pub fn annot_step(
   226      _pers: &PersTier,
   227      st: &mut AState,
   228      mode: &CheckMode,
   229      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   230      i: u64,
   231      fe: IFEnv,
   232      pend: Vec<PendingCheck>,
   233      pd: &IDeclaration,
   234  ) -> Result<(IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>), CheckError> {
   235      let vis: u64 = fe.visible_below;
   236      flush_caches(st);
   237      let mut tier: PersTier = enter_scratch(st);
   238      match annot_step_go(&tier, st, mode, pins, fe, pd) {
   239          Err(e) => {
   240              drop_scratch(st, tier);
   241              Err(e)
   242          }
   243          Ok((fe2, vg_opt)) => {
   244              let k: u64 = fe2.visible_below - vis;
   245              match vg_opt {
   246                  None => match promote_new(&mut tier, st, PMemo::empty(), CORE_WALK_FUEL, k, fe2) {
   247                      Err(e) => {
   248                          drop_scratch(st, tier);
   249                          Err(e)
   250                      }
   251                      Ok((_, fe3)) => {
   252                          drop_scratch(st, tier);
   253                          Ok((fe3, pend))
   254                      }
   255                  },
   256                  Some(vg) => annot_step_promote(tier, st, i, vis, k, fe2, pend, vg),
   257              }
   258          }
   259      }
   260  }
   261

   263  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:153-207 annotStep` — the
   264  /// bracket's `some vg` arm: the seam promoted first and the environment at the
   265  /// SAME memo, then the tier dropped and the record pushed.

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L529-L623
   529  
   530  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:440-457 checkDecls
   531  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/Run.lean:85-234 checkDeclsIO
   532  /// **The driver**: the two-phase fold with the boundary visible — a straight
   533  /// line of calls, with the observer's lines between them and the pool for
   534  /// phase B (tasks #97-P5-Driver, #98-POOL).  Each step is one premise of the capstone:
   535  ///
   536  /// | step | here | the capstone's premise |
   537  /// |---|---|---|
   538  /// | phase A | `checker::annot_fold_hooked(…, fold_start(), ds, 0, obs)` | the same call accepts |
   539  /// | boundary | `checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store)` | the same call's value |
   540  /// | phase B | `pool::parallel_all(m, workers, ‖ worker_state(pins), ‖w, k‖ check_pending(&tier, w, mode, &fe, &pend[k]), …)` | `h8`: index lists `ws` covering `0..pend.len`, each `w` a `foldlM` of `check_pending tier st mode fe pend[k]` over `k ∈ w` from `worker_state pins`, accepting (internally `ParallelAll`) |
   541  /// | after | `checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier)` | restores the store (`freeze_tier_ok`) |
   542  ///
   543  /// `init` and `step` are calls into the verified crate; `parallel_all` is the
   544  /// one trusted piece, and its contract (`pool.rs`'s note) is exactly
   545  /// `ParallelAll`: on `Ok`, every record was checked by some worker,
   546  /// each worker folding `check_pending` over the records it claimed on ONE
   547  /// `worker_state`.  Everything else here is the observer, which only ever
   548  /// holds `&` the state (the hook of phase A by the trait's own signature, the
   549  /// other lines through `&st.store` and the worker's `&AState`), so it cannot
   550  /// change an outcome.
   551  ///
   552  /// **The boundary is where the tier is FROZEN** (task #97-P6-6b).  Phase A
   553  /// owns its persistent tier and appends to it; at the boundary
   554  /// `checker::freeze_tier` moves the four stores' persistent tables out into
   555  /// one `PersTier`, handed back `frozen`: every read through it goes to those
   556  /// tables, and a worker's own store is frozen (`checker::worker_state`), so
   557  /// every append there is a scratch append (task #98-FREEZE).  The
   558  /// installed index goes to the workers by reference, since `check_pending`
   559  /// takes the visibility bound as a scalar — so `n` workers share one
   560  /// environment and one term DAG and own nothing but a scratch tier, their
   561  /// caches and a copy of the pin handles (`checker::worker_state`).
   562  pub fn check_decls_driver<O: PhaseObserver + InstallHook + Send>(
   563      pers: &PersTier,
   564      st: &mut AState,
   565      mode: &CheckMode,
   566      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   567      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   568      jobs: u64,
   569      obs: &mut O,
   570  ) -> Result<IFEnv, (CheckError, u64)> {
   571      let total = ds.len();
   572      // PHASE A (ConRon.Capstone: h6): the verified fold, the heartbeat as hook.
   573      let p = match checker::annot_fold_hooked(pers, st, mode, pins, checker::fold_start(), ds, 0, &*obs) {
   574          Err(e) => {
   575              obs.install_failed(e.1, total);
   576              return Err(e);
   577          }
   578          Ok(p) => p,
   579      };
   580      let (_n_installed, fe, pend): (u64, IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>) = p;
   581      let m = pend.len();
   582      obs.install_done(pers, &st.store, total, m);
   583      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   584      obs.phase_b_workers(workers);
   585      // THE PHASE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier leaves the state and becomes a
   586      // value every worker reads (the doc comment above).  `st` keeps its
   587      // (empty) store, its tables moved out, so the observer can still read a
   588      // label back through the tier.  (ConRon.Capstone: h7)
   589      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store);
   590      // PHASE B: `check_pending` at every record, on `workers` threads, each
   591      // folding it over the records it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the
   592      // verdict and the record a rejection names are the one-worker walk's at
   593      // every `--jobs` (the least failing index).  (ConRon.Capstone: h8)
   594      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   595      let lock: Mutex<(usize, &mut O)> = Mutex::new((0, obs));
   596      let r = parallel_all(
   597          m,
   598          workers,
   599          || checker::worker_state(&st.pins),
   600          |w: &mut AState, k| checker::check_pending(&tier, w, mode, &fe, &pend[k]),
   601          |w: &AState, k| check_line(heartbeat, &lock, &tier, w, m, &pend[k]),
   602      );
   603      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   604          Ok((_, o)) => o,
   605          Err(e) => e.into_inner().1,
   606      };
   607      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the fold — the verdict line's
   608      // declaration label, the failing record's name, the receipts — reads a
   609      // handle back out of `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has
   610      // gone out of scope answers `None` to every one of them (the first
   611      // version of this printed `at theorem ?` where the tip printed `at
   612      // theorem addOk`).  `thaw_tier` is `freeze_tier` inverted.
   613      checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   614      match phase_b_verdict(&pend, r) {
   615          Err((e, pos)) => {
   616              obs.check_failed(pos);
   617              Err((e, pos))
   618          }
   619          Ok(()) => {
   620              obs.check_done(m);
   621              Ok(fe)
   622          }
   623      }

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L30-L43
    30  //! ## What a worker is, in phase B
    31  //!
    32  //! §8.3 has said since P1 what phase B is: "the persistent tier is immutable
    33  //! in phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — **no atomics anywhere**",
    34  //! and task #97-P6-6 verified it in the code (`check_pending` is the bracket;
    35  //! the persistent interns' only caller is phase A's `arena::promote`, which
    36  //! writes a `&mut PersTier` a worker never holds).  So the driver's `init`
    37  //! builds `checker::worker_state(pins)` — an EMPTY store, FROZEN
    38  //! (`EStore::empty_frozen`: every append a scratch append), its own `Memos`
    39  //! and `Caches`, and a COPY of
    40  //! the driver's `Pins` — and its `step` borrows the frozen `&PersTier` and
    41  //! the installed `&IFEnv` (by reference: `check_pending` takes the record's
    42  //! prefix bound as a scalar, `pc.vis`, so a worker costs no environment copy
    43  //! at all — task #97-P6-6b).

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L721-L734
   721  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:180-196 checkWorker
   722  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Phased.lean:29-36 AState.worker` — the twin's
   723  /// phase-B worker reads the persistent tier where it is.
   724  /// **A phase-B worker's start state** (task #97-P6-6b's `pool::worker_state`,
   725  /// moved here by task #97-P5-Driver): the empty store, FROZEN
   726  /// (`EStore::empty_frozen`, task #98-FREEZE), so that every persistent read
   727  /// goes to the `PersTier` the boundary froze and every append is a scratch
   728  /// append; fresh memos and caches; and a copy of the pins.  The store stays
   729  /// frozen for the worker's life: `check_pending` only empties its scratch tier.
   730  pub fn worker_state(pins: &Pins) -> AState {
   731      let mut st = AState::init(EStore::empty_frozen());
   732      st.pins = pins_dup(pins);
   733      st
   734  }

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L227-L253
   227  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:207-245 checkPool
   228  /// **`step` at every index of `0..n`, on a pool of `workers` threads** — the
   229  /// module note's trusted claim is this function's contract:
   230  ///
   231  /// > If it returns `Ok(())`, every index in `0..n` was claimed by exactly one
   232  /// > worker, each worker built its state with `init()` once and folded `step`
   233  /// > over its claimed indices in claim order (increasing), and every step
   234  /// > returned `Ok(())`.
   235  ///
   236  /// On a failure it returns the LEAST failing index with its error
   237  /// (`ParallelError::Step`), whatever the timing.  `after(&st, k)` runs on the
   238  /// worker's thread after each step it made, with the worker's state by `&`
   239  /// (the driver's heartbeat); it cannot change an outcome.
   240  ///
   241  /// The workers are `std::thread::scope`d, with `STACK_BYTES` of stack each.
   242  /// `workers` is the count the caller has already clamped
   243  /// (`driver::workers_for`: `max(1, min(jobs, n))`); if the OS refuses to
   244  /// spawn one, the pool runs on those it has, and on the calling thread if it
   245  /// has none — the contract holds at every worker count, so the answer does
   246  /// not depend on it.
   247  pub fn parallel_all<S, E: Send>(
   248      n: usize,
   249      workers: usize,
   250      init: impl Fn() -> S + Sync,
   251      step: impl Fn(&mut S, usize) -> Result<(), E> + Sync,
   252      after: impl Fn(&S, usize) + Sync,
   253  ) -> Result<(), ParallelError<E>> {

== proof/ConRon/Arena/Denote.lean#L181-L206
   181  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:328-338 Expr — the fuel-indexed
   182  readback of an expression handle. -/
   183  def denoteEAux (st : EStore) : Nat → EIdx → Option Expr
   184    | 0, _ => none
   185    | f + 1, i =>
   186      (st.view i).bind fun v =>
   187        match v with
   188        | .bvar k => some (.bvar k)
   189        | .fvar k ty => (denoteEAux st f ty).map (Expr.fvar k)
   190        | .sort u => (denoteL st.ls u).map Expr.sort
   191        | .const n us => opt2 Expr.const (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteLs st.lss us)
   192        | .app g a => opt2 Expr.app (denoteEAux st f g) (denoteEAux st f a)
   193        | .lam ty b m =>
   194          opt2 (fun x y => Expr.lam x y m) (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   195        | .forallE ty b m =>
   196          opt2 (fun x y => Expr.forallE x y m) (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   197        | .letE ty w b =>
   198          opt3 Expr.letE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f w) (denoteEAux st f b)
   199        | .lit l => some (.lit l)
   200        | .proj n k e =>
   201          opt2 (fun nm x => Expr.proj nm k x) (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteEAux st f e)
   202  
   203  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:328-338 Expr — the readback of an
   204  expression handle, at the store's own node count as fuel. -/
   205  def denoteE (st : EStore) (i : EIdx) : Option Expr :=
   206    denoteEAux st (st.nodeCount + 1) i

== proof/ConRon/Arena/WF.lean#L1-L40
     1  /-
     2  # Store well-formedness and the store layer's theorems (DESIGN.md §8.3, P2a)
     3  
     4  `StoreWF` is the arena's own invariant — con-leche's `TWF`
     5  (`Setlec/Kernel/ArenaWF.lean:900`, 28 clauses) redrawn for the
     6  per-constructor, high-tag representation.  It lives here, beside the
     7  implementation, importing nothing from `ConRon.Refine`: con-leche's lesson 27,
     8  "implementation may import a *self-contained* data-structure verification".
     9  
    10  Each store's invariant is `∃ rank, …WFAt st rank`.  The rank is existential
    11  because nothing at runtime stores it (DESIGN §8.3: "zero runtime cost, and no
    12  global array order is needed with per-constructor arrays"); what it buys is
    13  
    14  * **acyclicity**, hence a terminating `denote`;
    15  * **a fuel bound**: a persistent node's rank is below the persistent node
    16    count and a scratch node's below the total, so `nodeCount + 1` — the fuel
    17    `denoteE` uses — is always enough, and `dropScratch` shrinks both sides of
    18    the persistent clause together.
    19  
    20  The clauses, in the order a reader meets them:
    21  
    22  | clause | what it says |
    23  |---|---|
    24  | `childOK` | every child is in range, ranked below its parent, and persistent if the parent is |
    25  | `rankP` / `rankS` | ranks are below the tier's node count (the fuel bound) |
    26  | `consP` / `consS` | each tier's cons table is exactly the inverse of that tier's `get` |
    27  | `fresh` | a scratch cons entry never duplicates a persistent one (DESIGN §8.3's cross-tier canonicity; con-leche's `t_cons_fresh`) |
    28  | `derExact` | the derived column is `derOfView` of the node — *locally*; the global `derived st i = e.data` is a theorem (`derived_exact`) |
    29  | `sized` | the derived array is as long as the node array |
    30  | `cap` | no constructor array exceeds 2^27 entries, so a handle's 27-bit index is injective on it |
    31  | `bmKey` | every binder key a cons table holds names a datum the store can decode |
    32  | `scrOff` | the scratch tier is empty while the scratch flag is off |
    33  | `sync` | the nesting's scratch flags move together (task #97a) |
    34  
    35  `childOK`'s third conjunct — *persistent parents have persistent children* —
    36  is what makes `dropScratch` sound: without it a persistent node could point
    37  into a tier that is about to vanish.  It needs no hypothesis at `intern`,
    38  because `scrOff` makes a scratch handle undecodable while the flag is off, so
    39  a valid child of a node appended to the persistent tier is persistent already.
    40  -/

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Specs.lean#L1-L62
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Bridge.Specs` — one `@[spec]` theorem per `Monad.lean` primitive
     3  
     4  The thing task #97s's spike exists to fix: **one spec theorem per (B)
     5  primitive, in one shape**, so that the verification-condition generator
     6  (`mvcgen` until task #111, `vcgen` since, on native `Std.WP` triples since
     7  task #111 slice 2) can walk a twin's body without any store reasoning
     8  appearing in the proof text.  The shape is the spike's
     9  seven-rule template (DESIGN §8.6, `P2s SPIKE`, and task #97s's own section):
    10  
    11  ```lean
    12  @[spec] theorem f_spec (s₀ : AState) (args…) (pre…) :
    13      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ f args ⦃fun r s' => Post s₀ r s'; ⊤⦄
    14  ```
    15  
    16  1. **the precondition is `s = s₀` and nothing else** — every real
    17     precondition is an ordinary hypothesis of the theorem, so `vcgen` turns it
    18     into a side goal instead of an entailment to discharge in the logic;
    19  2. **exception postcondition `⊤` (partial correctness), never the default
    20     `⊥`** (`⦃P⦄ x ⦃Q⦄` is TOTAL correctness in `Std.WP`) — a (B) function may
    21     fail and Theorem 1 claims nothing then (con-leche's `SimAt`,
    22     `Verify/SimI.lean:244`);
    23  3. **the postcondition names `s₀`**, the only way to state
    24     `Ext s₀.store s'.store` in a triple;
    25  4. **"the subject denotes" is an `isSome`, never a named `Expr`**;
    26  5. **the answer is a named relation** (`Bridge/Rel.lean`'s `RelE` family),
    27     never a bare `∀ e, … → …`;
    28  6. **a memo insert's spec states that the INVARIANT is preserved**, not that
    29     the table grew — the single highest-value change of the spike;
    30  7. **one named failure primitive** (`fail`), because a bare `throw` in
    31     `StateT σ (Except ε)` leaves `mvcgen` with universe metavariables.
    32  
    33  ## The frame conditions
    34  
    35  `AState` has four fields and the `Memos` record has thirteen tables, so a
    36  naive frame condition would be sixteen equations per spec.  Task #97b put the
    37  per-call tables in ONE record and task #97c the per-declaration ones in
    38  another for exactly this reason: every spec below frames the state in at most
    39  four equations, and a memo write frames the other twelve tables with one
    40  (`s'.memos = { s₀.memos with xC := … }`).
    41  
    42  `Bridge/StateOK.lean`'s `CheckOK.mono` is what those equations buy: the whole
    43  checker invariant crosses an `ExprOps` call on `Ext` plus
    44  `s'.caches = s₀.caches` plus `s'.pins = s₀.pins`.
    45  
    46  ## What is NOT here, and why
    47  
    48  * **`internPersistentE` / `…N` / `…L` / `…Ls`.**  `Arena/Store.lean`'s own
    49    note (the section "Interning into the PERSISTENT tier") states the
    50    obligation for the BRACKET and not for the operation: `internPersistent`
    51    breaks `fresh` transiently, and it is `promote … dropScratch` as a whole
    52    that takes `StoreWF` to `StoreWF`.  Its four specs therefore belong to the
    53    `Promote` tier, whose statement is that bracket, not to this file.
    54  * **the eleven `internRebuilt*` faces of `ExprOps.lean`** are here, at the
    55    end: they are `internE` plus task #97-P6-5's upward cutoff, and every
    56    rebuilding walk goes through them.
    57  
    58  ## The closer
    59  
    60  `bridge_vcs` at the end of this file is task #97s round 2's recipe: ONE
    61  curated `grind` list, a `bridge_peel` in front of it, and a second stage that
    62  puts the `RelE` transports back for the handful of verification conditions

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Run.lean#L59-L77
    59  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/SimI.lean:244 SimAt — **the PURE grade's
    60  statement**: from a well-formed store, an ACCEPTING run of the twin returns an
    61  answer related to the pure side's by `R`, having only grown the arena.
    62  
    63  Partial correctness, as everywhere in this library: a (B) function may fail
    64  and Theorem 1 claims nothing then — which is why the hypothesis is
    65  `c s0 = .ok (r, s')` and not an unconditional equation.

    69  induction rather than verification conditions, and `Bridge/Checker/Fold.lean`
    70  — the module that consumes `IndSpec` — is already written in run form

    73  branch; `Bridge/Inductives/Decl.lean`'s note says what that costs. -/

    49  /-! ## The core grade -/
    50  
    51  /-- con-leche: none — **the bridge between the two grades**: a pure step

    53  `CheckOK.mono`.  This is what lets a core-grade function call a pure-grade one

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/StructParts.lean#L118-L164
   118  /-! ## The spines -/
   119  
   120  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/StructParts.lean:52-53 structPsAt
   121  The parameter variables as seen from under `o` extra binders.
   122  
   123  **CLOSED** (task #97-P3-Ind round 2): a `Nat` recursion over
   124  `internBVarE_run` with the cursor `k` generalised.  The pure side is a
   125  `List.range` map, so the step is `List.range_succ_eq_map` and one `omega` on
   126  the index arithmetic (`k + (j + 1) = k + 1 + j`). -/
   127  theorem structPsAt_go_run (o nP : Nat) : ∀ (n k : Nat) {s s' : AState}
   128      {r : List EIdx}, StateOK s → Arena.structPsAt.go o nP n k s = .ok (r, s') →
   129      PStep s s' ∧ Frontend.denoteEList s'.store r
   130        = some ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j))) := by
   131    intro n
   132    induction n with
   133    | zero =>
   134      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   135      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   136      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok hrun
   137      exact ⟨PStep.refl hok, rfl⟩
   138    | succ n ih =>
   139      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   140      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   141      obtain ⟨b, s₁, h1, h2⟩ := AM.bind_ok hrun
   142      obtain ⟨rest, s₂, h3, h4⟩ := AM.bind_ok h2
   143      obtain ⟨hstep1, hb⟩ := internBVarE_run hok h1
   144      obtain ⟨hstep2, hrest⟩ := ih (k + 1) hstep1.ok h3
   145      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok h4
   146      refine ⟨hstep1.trans hstep2, ?_⟩
   147      have hkey : ((List.range (n + 1)).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j)))
   148          = Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - k) ::
   149            ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + 1 + j))) := by
   150        rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map]
   151        congr 1
   152        refine List.map_congr_left (fun j _ => ?_)
   153        simp only [Function.comp_apply]
   154        congr 1
   155        omega
   156      rw [hkey]
   157      simp only [Frontend.denoteEList, denote_ext hb hstep2.ext, hrest]
   158  
   159  theorem structPsAt_spec (o nP : Nat) :
   160      PSpec PT (Arena.structPsAt o nP) (REL (ConLeche.structPsAt o nP)) := by
   161    intro s₀ s' r hok _ hrun
   162    obtain ⟨hstep, hd⟩ := structPsAt_go_run o nP nP 0 hok hrun
   163    refine ⟨hstep, ?_⟩
   164    simpa only [ConLeche.structPsAt, Nat.zero_add] using hd

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L1-L30
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Refine2.Tactic.Lockstep` — the lockstep judgement and the `lockstep` tactic
     3  
     4  Task #97-T2-TACTIC.  Theorem 2 in its lockstep shape (task #97-T2-AUDIT §6)
     5  relates two programs doing the same operations in the same order, over a
     6  state relation that says only "the same data in two representations".  So a
     7  proof of one `_refines` lemma is a ZIP of two do-blocks: peel one bind on each
     8  side, close the correspondence of the two callees with a registered lemma,
     9  continue with the related results.  This file makes that zip a tactic.
    10  
    11  ## The judgement
    12  
    13  `LS pers R m lst x` — *every outcome of the Rust computation `m` is matched by
    14  the twin action `x` run from `lst`*: an `Ok a` by an `ok (b, lst')` with
    15  `R a b` in a related post-state, an `Err e` by the twin throwing at the same
    16  kind (`AErrSim`).  It is `Sim₀` with a relation for the answer instead of an
    17  abstraction function, and with the Rust equation moved into the judgement, so
    18  that the Rust program is visible in the GOAL beside the twin (`LS.toSim₀` is the
    19  bridge back).  Four companion judgements carry the other Rust callee shapes:
    20  
    21  | judgement | Rust callee shape | example |
    22  |---|---|---|
    23  | `LS`  | `Result (Result α CheckError × AState)` — state threaded | `intern_e_app`, a recursive call |
    24  | `LSR` | `Result (Result α CheckError)` — reads, may fail | `view` |
    25  | `LSV` | `Result α` — reads, total | `lift_get`, `inst_list_cutoff` |
    26  | `LSW` | `Result AState` — writes, total | `lift_set` |
    27  | `LSP` | `Result α`, **Rust only** — no twin counterpart | `fuel - 1#u64`, `dup2`, `eidx_nat_key`, `fail` |
    28  | `LSM` | `Result (Result α × AState × M)` — a memoised walk, memo beside the result | `consts_resolve_f_go`, `intern_expr_go` |
    29  | `LSRM` | `Result (Result α × M)` — a memoised reader walk | `all_level_params_defined_go` |
    30  

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L164-L168
   164  /-- **The lockstep judgement** for a state-threading Rust computation. -/
   165  def LS {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   166      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState))
   167      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   168    ∀ o st', m = ok (o, st') → LOut pers R o st' (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L170-L174
   170  /-- A Rust READ that may fail: the state is `st` before and after. -/
   171  def LSR {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   172      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError))
   173      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   174    ∀ o, m = ok o → LOut pers R o st (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L634-L646
   634  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised state walk**: `LS` of the walk with
   635  its memo moved into the answer; `R` relates `(answer, memo)` to the twin's
   636  answer (typically the twin's `(answer, memo)` pair). -/
   637  def LSM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   638      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState × M))
   639      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   640    LS pers R (packM m) lst x
   641  
   642  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised reader walk** at the state `st`. -/
   643  def LSRM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   644      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × M))
   645      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   646    LS pers R (packRM st m) lst x

  2871  macro "lockstep" : tactic => `(tactic| repeat' lockstep_step)

    87  initialize registerBuiltinAttribute {
    88    name := `lockstep
    89    descr := "a lockstep correspondence lemma, keyed on its Rust callee; \
    90      `@[lockstep high]` / `@[lockstep <n>]` sets its priority"
    91    add := fun decl stx kind => do

== proof/ConRon/Refine/Abs.lean#L536-L559
   536  /-- `ConLeche/Kernel/PropWhen.lean:360-384` -- the canonical-form invariant of
   537  the sealed datum, in the same shape as `NameWF`/`LevelWF`.
   538  
   539  con-leche's `PropWhenRepr` carries it as proof *fields* (`two p q` needs
   540  `p < q`, `many ps` needs `PropWhen.Sorted ps ∧ 2 < ps.length`), which Charon
   541  erases (task #9, item 3); here they come back as the four smart constructors
   542  that are the port's only way in — `prop_when::never`, `prop_when::if_all_zero`,
   543  `prop_when::inter` and `prop_when::bind_z` (the module's whole set of public
   544  producers; `of_sorted`/`two_prime` are Rust-private).  Canonical sortedness by
   545  the port's own `prop_when::name_cmp` is therefore not *stated* but *derived*:
   546  `ConRon/Refine/PropWhen.lean`'s `wf_shape` turns a `PropWhenWF` derivation
   547  into the invariant `WFShape` — well-formed names, a strictly ascending
   548  abstracted parameter list, and a `Many` that really holds more than two
   549  names — and that is what makes `to_list` and `beq` exact.
   550  
   551  The `bind_z` constructor quantifies over the dictionary type `F`: the port's
   552  stand-in for `bindZ`'s function argument (task #9, pattern 1). -/
   553  inductive PropWhenWF : prop_when.PropWhen → Prop where
   554    | never {pw} : prop_when.never = ok pw → PropWhenWF pw
   555    | if_all_zero {ps pw} : NamesWF ps → prop_when.if_all_zero ps = ok pw → PropWhenWF pw
   556    | inter {a b pw} : PropWhenWF a → PropWhenWF b → prop_when.inter a b = ok pw → PropWhenWF pw
   557    | bind_z {F : Type} {inst : prop_when.NameToPw F} {f : F} {pw c} :
   558        (∀ n, NameWF n → ∀ r, inst.apply f n = ok r → PropWhenWF r) →
   559        PropWhenWF pw → prop_when.bind_z inst f pw = ok c → PropWhenWF c

   655        args.val.length - i.val = n → AStateRel₀ pers st lst → AStateInv pers st →
   656        LS pers (fun a b => b = absEIdx a) (arena.expr_ops.inst_spine_from pers st fuel args i t e) lst

   668  @[lockstep] theorem inst_spine_from_ls {pers st lst} (hrel : AStateRel₀ pers st lst)
   669      (hinv : AStateInv pers st) (fuel : Std.U64) (args : alloc.vec.Vec arena.handle.EIdx) (i : Std.Usize) (t : Std.U64) (e : arena.handle.EIdx) :
